system_overview: This specification models the N-Queens problem, a classic combinatorial puzzle that asks how to place N chess queens on an N-by-N chessboard such that no two queens threaten each other. The specification defines what constitutes a valid solution and provides an iterative algorithm that systematically constructs all solutions by extending partial placements one row at a time.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a single solver process that maintains a work set of partial queen placements and a result set of completed solutions. Each placement assigns one queen per row, recording which column that queen occupies. The solver repeatedly picks a partial placement, attempts to extend it by one row, and either produces a complete solution or generates new partial placements for further extension.
state_variables: The system tracks two collections: (1) a set of partial placements still to be processed, where each partial placement is an ordered list of column positions shorter than the board size, and (2) a set of completed solutions found so far, where each solution is an ordered list of column positions of length equal to the board size.
initial_state: The work set contains a single empty placement (no queens placed yet). The result set is empty (no solutions found).
actions: The solver selects any partial placement from the work set, determines which row to fill next, and computes all columns where a queen can be placed without conflicting with any previously placed queen. A conflict occurs when two queens share the same column or lie on the same diagonal. For each valid column, the solver creates an extended placement. If the extended placement covers all rows, it is added to the result set; otherwise, it is added to the work set. The original partial placement is removed from the work set.
safety_properties: The result set contains only valid solutions at all times: every completed placement in the result set has no two queens attacking each other. When the work set becomes empty, the result set contains all possible solutions.
liveness_properties: The work set eventually becomes empty, meaning the algorithm terminates and all solutions have been found.
model_bounds: The board size N is a constant positive natural number. For model checking, N must be instantiated with a specific finite value (typically small values like 4 or 5, since the state space grows rapidly).
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on the solver's extension action, ensuring the algorithm continues making progress as long as there are partial placements remaining. The board size must be at least 1.
